harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Repaired `/srv/legacy2/large-counter-overflow/bin/total.py`. It now sums nonnegative decimal counters with arbitrary precision, rejects negative or malformed records without emitting a partial total, remains executable, and persists across reboot. Alpine 3.23.3 and kernel 6.18.7-0-lts were unchanged.
actions_performed: Replaced the fixed-width signed conversion with an architecture-independent POSIX shell implementation using the installed BusyBox arbitrary-precision `bc`.
Added full-record validation before publishing output.
Verified totals above 4 GiB and the signed 64-bit range.
Verified negative and malformed inputs exit nonzero with zero stdout.
Restarted node1 safely and verified application, data, networking, and required services recovered.

evidence.summary: Produced 4,294,967,303 from the supplied counters, 8,589,934,592 above 4 GiB, and exact totals beyond signed 64-bit range before and after restart.

evidence.requirement: Reject invalid or negative records without partial output
evidence.summary: Negative, malformed, and supplied-invalid inputs returned status 1 with zero-byte stdout, including after restart.

evidence.requirement: Preserve counter-file and integer-decimal interface on installed architecture
evidence.summary: The installed x86_64-compatible BusyBox calculator demonstrated arbitrary-precision decimal behavior; the executable accepts a counter-file argument and emits one decimal integer.

Captured healthy baseline boot ID and services, received restart acknowledgement, observed boot ID change from 593954a6-fd5a-444b-9f3b-80c8e48fca50 to 7b9d005a-8461-4b50-bfa2-e34e0b308136, then verified checksums, application behavior, network state, and all required services.
